page: Amazon Web Services i7ie.3xlarge is a storage-optimized server powered by an Intel Xeon 8559C processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 12 dedicated vCPUs across 6 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, running at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The CPU includes a 320 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The instance is equipped with 96.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core.

For high-throughput storage requirements, the server includes 7500 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. This storage is bundled directly with the instance, operating under the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps. There are no complimentary public IPv4 addresses included with this instance type.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier performance in specific single-threaded workloads. The server achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 2307.0 and a text processing score of 2928.0, both placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also show strong performance in the top 25%, reaching 34.64 GB/sec and 14.29 GB/sec respectively. For machine learning workloads, LLM text generation using a small 135M model reaches a top-tier speed of 382.91 tokens/sec, while larger model inference and multi-core operations generally perform in the average range.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the i7ie.3xlarge offers high resource density by combining a substantial 7500 GB local NVMe storage allocation with 96.0 GB of DDR5 memory. This hardware profile is optimized for data-intensive workloads that require rapid local read/write access and significant memory capacity without the overhead of external storage attachments. Appropriate workloads include relational and non-relational databases, local data caching, text processing pipelines, and small-scale machine learning inference.
